answer: According to the Data For Good white paper (Document ID = 6), in the case of a Meta translation model studied by Wu et al. (2022), over a two-year period, the impact of the training phase corresponded to 35% of the total footprint, while the remaining 65% of the footprint came from the inference phase (serving predictions). Thus, 65% of the model's two-year footprint came from serving predictions rather than learning.
